posts.author: Kris Meerlo
posts.content_md:
Some pictures from my new home made coating machine:

Some specifications:

-Temp control ( roomtemp to 70 C )

-Variable speed control.

-cooling with fans.

For the temp control I use the amazing sauna belt from amazing discoveries incl a digital temp controller from Conrad electronics.

For quick cooling off the aluminium heating plate I use harddisc drive cooling fans.

I tape the heat tracing from the Sauna belt on the Alu plate with heat resistance alu tape.

The movement of the meyerbar is variable.

( I "stole" some ideas for the coating machine from the internet ).

And I have some ideas from Hans.

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md:
Here is my version. Not as nice as yours, but still works fine. In the background are the two homemade meyerbars.

![Image](http://hologramhans.hopto.org/pictures/Coating-Machine.jpg)

One problem I have found with my machine is the following:

If I use normal glass that has only been cleaned with Glassex window cleaner, the machine produces a nice and flat coating. 

But if I pre-treat the glass with silane, the glass becomes hydrophobic. This has a negative effect on the flatness of the coating because the gelatin wants to run of the glass in any direction it can while it is still liquid.

hans, does the film act any different ,(widex vs saline). if somthing works use it and dont look back!

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md:
> hans, does the film act any different ,(widex vs saline). if somthing works use it and dont look back!

Yes. If I don't silane, the film detaches in the wash bath if washed too long. Films that are not extremely thin need long washing times in MBDCG to get all the chemicals out. That is the reason why I am experimenting with F5 fixer now to harden the emulsion and to more quickly wash the chemicals out.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: I am not sure what the difference between MBDCG and DCG is such that there is emulsion lift problems. I have kept my emulsion in water for 10 minutes or more at times and I have never once in my life seen emulsion lift from the glass. I soak my glass, either fresh or with an old DCG emulsion on it in a 5% solution of hydrochloric acid (Muratic Acid) over night or longer. Then wash with water twice and before it is completely dry, finich drying with a paper towel.
